stimulus.text:
The painting shows the French Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen (1789) as two stone tablets, like the tablets of the law. Above them shines the Eye of Providence in a triangle. At the left, a woman holds the broken chains of tyranny; at the right, a winged figure holds a sceptre. Article I reads (in French): “Men are born and remain free and equal in rights.”
— Jean-Jacques-François Le Barbier (attributed), Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, c. 1789, Musée Carnavalet, Paris

books.section: Topic 3.6 The Influence of Revolutionary Ideals, C. The Impact of the American Revolution Abroad

primary_sources: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen (August 26, 1789)

stem: Article I's claim that men “are born and remain free and equal in rights” most directly echoes

options.text: The American Declaration's claim that “all men are created equal”
The British claim that Parliament alone could tax the colonies
options.misconception: Parliament's claim was about authority over the colonies, not about men being born free and equal.

options.text: The Virginia Convention's threat to punish enslaved people who fled
options.misconception: Virginia's threat punished flight; Article I proclaims equality, the opposite of a threat.

options.text: The Loyalist claim that only the king could protect colonial rights
options.misconception: Loyalists looked to the king for protection; Article I grounds rights in nature, not in a monarch.

rationales.A: The French words repeat the American idea: equality is natural and birthright, not a gift from a king. Background: French revolutionaries borrowed the American example and the same Enlightenment language.
rationales.B: Parliament's tax claim asserts power over subjects; Article I asserts rights that belong to men by birth.
rationales.C: Virginia's punishment defends slavery; Article I declares the equality that slavery denies.
rationales.D: A king's protection is granted from above; Article I says rights belong to men by nature, not by royal gift.
rationales.general:
1. Read Article I. Men are born and remain free and equal in rights.
2. Read the American line. Background: “All men are created equal” states the same claim, in the same words of nature.
3. Rule out the rest. Parliament, Virginia's threats, and Loyalist loyalty all assert power, not natural equality.
Remember: an echo is a shared idea in shared words — match the claim, not only the date.
